prompt:
UI design mockup of the project screen of an AI software factory console, in its existing "Mission control" design: a near-black blue room (dark) or a warm cream day version (light), thin-bordered instrument panels with small corner marks, cyan as the system colour, amber as the one signal that needs a person, monospace figures, everything exact and calm. Desktop browser viewport, 16:9, flat, no browser chrome, no device frame, the screen fills the whole image.

The shell is fixed and must look like this: a quiet top bar ("Factory console", the project "ai-software-factory-code", links "Board", "New task", "Projects", "Resources", "Costs", "Policy", "Alerts", a small moon-and-sun theme selector in a thin frame, "sebastian", "Log out"); under it the pulse band, one panel with the sentence "Two cards need your decision; #612's merge carries a migration." with an amber warning sign and a 3 px amber left rule, and under the sentence the instrument strip "● waiting on you | 3 working | 2 need you | €61.40 / €120.00 ▬▬▬▭▭ 51 % | GitHub: 1 open pull request | ▾"; then the main area: the chat on the left taking 40 percent of the width as the main region, with a narrow mono table of threads at its left edge ("Inbox" first with a small house mark, "Plan: the members page" with a cyan dot, "Session store: Postgres" as the open row, "Costs read: the date window") and the open thread's log and composer at its right (the box "Ask or tell the project…", "Send", small chips "/compact" "/new", and a small level button "assisted" under Send); and the board on the right taking 60 percent with its header row "Board", a small mono text box "Find: a word, #612, plan:558", "Wide view" and "?", and four columns: "Needs you 2" lit amber (a merge approval "Merge PR #612" with chips "high risk" "migration" and buttons "Approve", "Deny", "Split"; a question "#603 Which store for the session table?" with buttons "Postgres", "SQLite", "Ask the author"), "Queued 4", "In progress 5", "Done 8", each column head with a small ▾ at its right, the cards compact with a mono state row. No ticker at the foot.

What is new, and what this image is about: the factory runs routines, recurring work on a clock, and the member must see them before they file a card. The moment is Monday 05:40. The routines of this project, spelled exactly: "Weekly bump" · every Monday 06:00 · human card · next in 20 min · last Mon 6 Oct #781 merged; "Template pass" · hourly · pull request · last 05:03 no change; "Dependency update" · every Thursday 06:00 · agent card · next Thu · last Thu 9 Oct #779 merged; "Audit" · after 20 merges · agent card · 14 of 20 · last 2 Oct #702 3 findings. Two jobs of the cluster: "Backup" · daily 02:00 · last ok; "Forgejo dump" · daily 02:30 · last ok. In the Done column two cards carry a small mono chip "↻ routine": "#781 Weekly bump of the pinned outside inputs" and "#779 Dependency update". The acts on a routine are "Skip once" and "Run now" as small quiet buttons. A change of rhythm is proposed in the chat as a configuration change, never as a toggle.

Direction "Panel column": The instrument strip is expanded: under it, inside the pulse band, the status panel shows four quiet columns split by hairlines with small-capitals heads in the faint colour: "In progress" (three card lines like "#601 Console: the drawer's Overview · building · 23 min"), "Needs you" (two lines), "Spend" (two small gauges "€4.82 of €10.00 day cap", "€61.40 of €120.00 month cap"), and the fourth column titled "Routines": one mono row per routine, "Weekly bump · Mon 06:00 · in 20 min", "Template pass · hourly · 05:03 no change", "Dependency update · Thu 06:00 · #779 merged", "Audit · after 20 merges · 14 of 20", then a hairline and "Backup 02:00 ok · Forgejo dump 02:30 ok" in the faint colour, and at the column's foot the configuration row "configuration v214 · a1f9c3e · provider ok · GitHub 1 open". The chat and the board below are unchanged and a little shorter. Light theme: the cream day version of the same design, dark navy text on warm off-white panels, the same cyan and amber.

Legible UI text with exact spelling, nothing invented, no lorem ipsum. The pulse stays the loudest thing on the screen after the amber Needs you column; the chat stays the main region; the routines are quiet instruments in the muted colour, and the only loud marks are the ones the shell already has. Made by a top product design studio. Not a template, not a generic admin dashboard.
label: 02-panel-column-light · nano-banana
